title: Effect set · Four surfaces
premise: Four textures, each a counted mark. None of them a gradient. Rebuilt on white with the dials that change how the marks are made — count, dropoff, color rule, edge — never the zoom of a tile.
source: Mindgut · Technique & Front-End Study V01 §08 (texture recipes) · ø co. · 2026-10-23

color.gamut: sRGB; out-of-gamut inks have chroma reduced at constant L and h (binary search, 24 steps)

mix.oklch: L, C linear; hue on the short arc; achromatic end takes the other hue

overprint.multiply: transparent inks; product in linear light
overprint.mix: opaque; blended by the mix space
overprint.darken: OKLab: lower L, top ink a/b

units: CSS px for every length; rendered at device px (dpr ≤ 2). Density params change mark count per px², never a tile scale.

shared.blueNoise: 64 × 64 void-and-cluster rank tile, σ 1.9, toroidal, seed 1993
shared.mask: signed distance to rect | ellipse | band | blob, displaced by fbm (wander, scale, octaves), feather as tone or blue-noise speckle, bite = clumped dropouts rising toward the edge; cached by params

effects.name: Stipple ramp
effects.sub: Tone made of whole dots. Value sets how many sites print (FM) or how big each dot is (AM); a blue-noise rank decides which sites, so sparse areas thin evenly.
recipe: Lay a site lattice at the pitch (CSS px). Jitter each site inside its cell.
Read the value field at the site: linear ramp, radial, or noise — eased from → to by the dropoff curve.
Screen: FM keeps a site when its rank < value; AM keeps every site and sets radius ∝ √value. The FM↔AM dial interpolates.
Rank comes from a 64 × 64 void-and-cluster tile (blue), a hash (white), or Bayer 8 × 8 (ordered).
Rasterize each kept dot analytically (7 vertex radii, AA by distance) into a coverage layer, then mix ink into the ground per pixel in the chosen color space. Ink B overprints by the overprint rule.
The mask is sampled at the site, not the pixel: dots are whole or absent, never sliced by the edge.

limits.what: sites merge into flat tone at 1× — the stipple stops reading as marks
dots overlap into a solid; FM loses its range
clumps and voids at low density — the original jittered-hash look
radius steps quantize to the pixel grid; banding

effects.name: Ink leaving paper
effects.sub: A solid that runs out. Coverage eases off across a warped edge; inside the transition it resolves to binary speckle (blue-noise threshold, optionally streaked along the stroke), with starved pinholes and film mottle in the body.
recipe: Distance to the edge line along the stroke direction (CSS px), displaced by fbm warp.
Coverage = dropoff curve over the transition width.

Speckle: perturb coverage by a clump noise (clump size, stretched along the stroke by streak), then threshold it per device pixel against the blue-noise rank. Speckle 0 → continuous tone, 1 → pure binary.
Starve: clumped pinholes, likelier where coverage is thin. Mottle: low-frequency film thickness, taken off coverage.
Mask × coverage × ink density, mixed into the ground per pixel in the chosen color space.

limits.what: reads as a hard vector edge — no speckle band to see
clumps read as blotches, not ink
the edge becomes a gradient — the "AI gradient" failure
marks read as scanlines unless the angle is off-axis

effects.name: Paper tooth
effects.sub: White stock that is not a screen. On white, tooth can only take light away, so it is built as depth: a height field shaded by flat value or a raking light, plus laid fibers and pits, all as an OKLab L offset with an optional tint in the pits.
recipe: Height field = fbm at the tooth scale; octaves and persistence set the spectrum (how fast detail drops off).
Distribution curve reshapes height (more valleys, or more peaks). Rake mixes flat value with relief lit from the light angle (finite-difference gradient).
Fibers: curved strokes at a count per 100 × 100 px, laid near the grain angle with spread; pits: small dots. Both rasterized into separate coverage channels.
Depth = amplitude × shade (+ fibers, pits), optionally stronger toward the plate edges by the falloff curve.
Shade: L −= depth in OKLab (a/b pulled toward the tint by depth) — or multiply in linear / sRGB, for comparison.

limits.what: collapses into per-pixel noise — digital grain, not paper
the same depth looks ~2× stronger than in linear; keep oklab for predictable steps

effects.name: Weave
effects.sub: Cloth, built as cloth: warp and weft threads with their own counts, a real interlacing pattern, slubbed thread width, cylindrical shading along every float, under-threads in shadow, whole accent threads and worn floats.
recipe: Warp columns and weft rows at their own counts (threads per 100 CSS px); each thread gets a jittered center, a thickness, a dye-lot L offset, and accent membership.
Interlacing pattern decides which thread is on top at each crossing; a float is the run of crossings where it stays on top.
Thread half-width = fill × pitch / 2, modulated along its length by slub noise. AA coverage from distance to the centerline.
Shading in OKLab L: across the thread (cylinder) and along the float (dives under at both ends); the under-thread sits in shadow.
Wear thins and fades floats with a probability that rises along the wear direction by its curve; a worn float shows more of the thread beneath and the ground through the gap.

limits.what: threads under 2.5 px alias against the display — moiré
reads as a grid of strokes, not cloth
gutters close; the weave flattens to a check
accents stop being accents — a plaid

usages.title: Meter · counted marks
usages.sub: Three readings as stipple fields. Value is the share of the bar that prints; the bar's end runs out by the dropoff curve instead of a hard cap.

usages.title: Ticket · ink over tooth
usages.sub: Paper tooth as the ground, then the ink edge printed over it in a band: the solid gives out into speckle before the stub line.

usages.title: Swatch · frayed patch
usages.sub: Weave inside a blob mask with a wide speckle feather and bite: the cut edge frays instead of ending on a vector line. Tooth underneath.

usages.title: Headline · ink runs out of the word
usages.sub: Type rasterized as a clip; the ink edge crosses it, so the last letters print starved. Type is a mask, never a gradient fill.

usages.title: Overprint · two inks, one rule
usages.sub: Two stipple ramps crossing on a radial field. Where they meet, the overprint rule and the mix space decide the third color — switch them on FX-01 and watch this card.

usages.title: Image slot · placeholder
usages.sub: A generated slot for a layout: noise-driven stipple inside a rounded rect, so a template never ships a gray box. Replace with a real image.
